items.subject: Maths
items.text: Find the smallest number that is divisible by each of 8, 9 and 10.

items.subject: Maths
items.text:
You have a piece of construction paper that measures 32 cm by 48 cm. You want to cut it into squares of equal size.
(i) What will be the dimensions of the largest possible square?
(ii) How many such squares will you have?

items.subject: Maths
items.text: If α and β are the zeroes of the quadratic polynomial f(x) = 6x² + 11x − 10, find the value of α/β + β/α.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Find the zeroes of 4x² – 3x – 1 by factorisation and verify the relationship between zeroes and coefficients.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: The sum of two numbers is 85. When the larger number is divided by the smaller, the quotient is 3 and the remainder is 5. Find the two numbers.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Shalvi wants to use milk and orange juice to increase calcium and vitamin A in her diet. One ounce of milk contains 38 mg of calcium and 56 micrograms of vitamin A. One ounce of orange juice contains 5 mg of calcium and 60 micrograms of vitamin A. How many ounces of milk and orange juice should she drink each day to provide exactly 550 mg of calcium and 1200 micrograms of vitamin A?

items.subject: Maths
items.text: A two-digit number is four times the sum of its digits and also twice the product of its digits. Find the number.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: (A) Find the sum and product of the roots of the quadratic equation 2x2 – 9x + 4 = 0. 2 OR (B) Find the discriminant of the quadratic equation 4x2 – 5 = 0 and hence comment on the nature of roots of the equation.

items.subject: Maths
items.text:
A machine bought for ₹1,00,000 loses a fixed ₹8,000 of value every year. Its values at the end of years 1, 2, 3, … are ₹92000, ₹84000, ₹76000, …
(i) What is the common difference of the value AP?
(ii) What is the machine's value at the end of year 5?
(iii) At the end of which year is the value ₹36,000?
(iv) By how much does the year-2 value exceed the year-6 value?

items.subject: Maths
items.text:
Potted plants are arranged in 12 rows on a stepped stand: 3 pots in row 1 and 4 more in each higher row: 3, 7, 11, …
(i) What is the common difference of the pots AP?
(ii) How many pots are in row 10?
(iii) Given the top (12th) row, find the total number of pots on the stand.
(iv) Which row has exactly 27 pots?

items.subject: Maths
items.text: If in two right triangles one of the acute angles of one triangle is equal to an acute angle of the other triangle, can the two triangles be similar? Why?

items.subject: Maths
items.text: ABCD is a trapezium in which AB ∥ DC and its diagonals intersect at the point O. Show that AO/BO = CO/DO.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the line segment joining the points (5, −6) and (−1, −4). Also find the point of intersection.

items.subject: Maths
items.text:
In a school morning assembly, students stand in rows and columns forming a coordinate grid. Four friends Amar(A), Bharat(B), Colin(C) and Dravid(D) stand at A(3, 4), B(6, 7), C(9, 4) and D(6, 1).
(i) What is the distance between A and B?
(ii) What is the distance between C and D?
(iii) What is the distance between A and C?
(iv) What is the distance between D and B?

items.subject: Maths
items.text: The shadow of a tower standing on level ground is 40 m longer when the Sun's altitude is 30° than when it is 60°. Find the height of the tower.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Find the angle of elevation of the Sun when the shadow of a pole h metres high is √3 h metres long.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: PQ and PR are two tangents to a circle with centre O and radius 5 cm. AB is another tangent to the circle at C which lies on OP. If OP = 13 cm, then find the length AB and PA.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: If d₁ and d₂ (with d₂ > d₁) are the diameters of two concentric circles and c is the length of a chord of the larger circle that is tangent to the smaller circle, prove that d₂² = c² + d₁².

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Find the area of the minor segment of a circle of radius 14 cm, when the angle of the corresponding sector is 60°.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: With vertices A, B and C of a right triangle ABC (right-angled at B) as centres, arcs of radius 5 cm each are drawn. If AB = 14 cm, BC = 48 cm and CA = 50 cm, find the area of the shaded region inside the triangle but outside the three sectors.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: State whether true or false and justify: 'Two identical solid hemispheres of equal base radius r cm are stuck together along their bases. The total surface area of the combination is 6πr².'

items.subject: Maths
items.text: A vessel is in the form of an inverted cone of height 8 cm and top radius 5 cm, open at the top and filled with water to the brim. Lead shots — each a sphere of radius 0.5 cm — are dropped in, and one-fourth of the water flows out. Find the number of lead shots dropped into the vessel. (Take π = 22/7.)

items.subject: Maths
items.text:
Compute the median of the following data:
Mid-value : Frequency
115 : 12
125 : 15
135 : 20
145 : 16
155 : 10
165 : 16
175 : 11

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Design a grouped frequency distribution over four equal classes of width 10 (starting at 0) such that the mode is exactly 25. Specify the frequencies and verify using the mode formula.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: In a game the entry fee is ₹5. The game consists of tossing a coin 3 times. If one or two heads show, Sweta gets her entry fee back; if she throws 3 heads she gets double the entry fee; otherwise she loses. For tossing a coin three times, find the probability that she (i) loses the entry fee, (ii) gets double the entry fee, (iii) just gets her entry fee back.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: The king, queen and ace of clubs and diamonds are removed from a deck of 52 playing cards and the remaining cards are shuffled. A card is randomly drawn from the remaining cards. Find the probability of getting (i) a card of clubs. (ii) a red coloured card.

items.subject: Science
items.text: (i) Why is acidified water considered to be a good conductor of electricity ? (ii) Write a chemical equation showing the ionic products formed on dissolving potassium hydroxide in water. (iii) Care must be taken while diluting concentrated nitric acid with water. Why ? 3 3 3 3 3 16

items.subject: Science
items.text: Grapes hanging on the plant do not ferment but after being plucked from the plant can be fermented. Under what conditions do these grapes ferment? Is it a chemical or a physical change?

items.subject: Science
items.text: Describe an activity to illustrate that the reaction of a metal carbonate or hydrogencarbonate with an acid produces carbon dioxide. Write the equations and name two forms in which calcium carbonate occurs in nature.

items.subject: Science
items.text: Arrange the following in increasing order of their pH values: NaOH solution, blood, lemon juice.

items.subject: Science
items.text:
Give the formulae of the stable binary compounds that would be formed by the combination of following pairs of elements.
(a) Mg and N₂
(b) Li and O₂
(c) Al and Cl₂
(d) K and O₂

items.subject: Science
items.text:
Three oxides are tested with litmus dissolved in water: sodium oxide (Na2O) turns red litmus blue; carbon dioxide (CO2) turns blue litmus red; aluminium oxide (Al2O3) reacts with both an acid and a base.
(i) Classify Na2O as acidic, basic or amphoteric.
(ii) Classify CO2.
(iii) Classify Al2O3.
(iv) In general, metal oxides are of which nature and non-metal oxides of which nature?

items.subject: Science
items.text: What are the two properties of carbon which lead to the huge number of carbon compounds we see around us?

items.subject: Science
items.text: Write the molecular formula of 2nd and the 3rd member of homologous series whose first member is methane.

items.subject: Science
items.text: When sunlight is concentrated at a paper placed at the principal focus of a convex lens, what happens to the paper? Why?

items.subject: Science
items.text: Differentiate between reflection and refraction of light.

items.subject: Science
items.text: Is the position of a star as seen by us its true position? Justify your answer.

items.subject: Science
items.text: Mention the factor on which scattering of light depends. Why does the sky appear dark in space?

items.subject: Science
items.text: Kaveri connected a bulb A (100 Ω) to a 240 V supply. (a) How much energy will be consumed if it is kept ON for 4 hours each day for a week? Express in kJ. (b) She then connects another similar bulb B in series with A across 240 V. Will the brightness of A change? Explain mathematically.

items.subject: Science
items.text: Compare the power used in the 2 Ω resistor in each of the following circuits: (i) a 6 V battery in series with 1 Ω and 2 Ω resistors, and (ii) a 4 V battery in parallel with 12 Ω and 2 Ω resistors.

items.subject: Science
items.text: A circular coil carries a current that flows anticlockwise when the coil is viewed from its front face. Draw the magnetic field lines for this coil. Decide which of its faces behaves as the North pole and which face as the South pole. Give reason to justify your answer.

items.subject: Science
items.text: Meena draws magnetic field lines of field close to the axis of a current carrying circular loop. As she moves away from the centre of the circular loop she observes that the lines keep on diverging. How will you explain her observation.

items.subject: Science
items.text: How is nutrition in a fungus different from that in a tapeworm?

items.subject: Science
items.text: Design an experiment to demonstrate hydrotropism.

items.subject: Science
items.text: What constitutes the central and peripheral nervous systems? How are the components of central nervous system protected?

items.subject: Science
items.text: What could be the TWO most likely reasons for unicellular organisms to reproduce only through asexual reproduction?

items.subject: Science
items.text: How does binary fission differ from multiple fission?

items.subject: Science
items.text: An angiosperm plant having red coloured flowers when crossed with the other having the same colour produced 40 progenies, out of which 30 plants were with red coloured flowers, 10 plants were with white coloured flowers. Find out: a. What is the possible genotype of parent plants? b. Which trait is dominant and recessive? c. What is this cross called as and what is its phenotypic ratio?

items.subject: Science
items.text: How do Mendel's experiments show that the a. traits may be dominant or recessive, b. traits are inherited independently?

items.subject: Science
items.text: What are decomposers ? List two important roles they play in the environment.

items.subject: Science
items.text: Marked decline in the thickness of ozone layer was noticed in the 1980s. Which human activity can be held accountable for this change? What is the possible effect of this on human health?

items.subject: Maths
items.text: If cosec θ + cot θ = p, prove that cos θ = (p² − 1)/(p² + 1).

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Prove that: (sin^4 θ − cos^4 θ + 1) cosec^2 θ = 2. OR If sin x + cosec x = 2, then find the value of sin^19 x + cosec^20 x.

items.text: Prove the identity: sec²θ + cosec²θ · √(... )  ⇒ Prove that sec²θ + cosec²θ ≥ tan θ + cot θ, equivalently establish that sec²θ + cosec²θ = (tan θ + cot θ)² · 1 …  [Actually prove:]  Prove √(sec²θ + cosec²θ) = tan θ + cot θ.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: If tan A = 3/4, show that sin A · cos A = 12/25.

items.subject: Maths
items.text:
Two square tiles have side lengths (in cm) equal to the zeros of x² − 7x + 10. A new pattern uses tiles whose sides equal the AREAS of the original tiles (i.e. the squares of the original zeros).
(i) Find the original side lengths (the zeros).
(ii) Write the new side lengths (the squares of the zeros).
(iii) State the sum and product of the new zeros.
(iv) Form a quadratic whose zeros are the squared values.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: A train covers a distance of 300 km at a uniform speed. On a foggy day it travelled 10 km/h slower than usual and therefore took 1 hour longer for the journey. Find the train's usual speed.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: The 5th term of an AP is 20 and the sum of its 7th and 11th terms is 64. Find the common difference.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: There is a circular path around a sports field. Sonia takes 18 minutes to drive one round of the field, while Ravi takes 12 minutes for the same. Suppose they both start at the same point and at the same time, and go in the same direction. After how many minutes will they meet again at the starting point?

items.subject: Science
items.text: Define absolute refractive index. Absolute refractive indices of medium A and medium B are n_a and n_b respectively. What is the refractive index of medium B with respect to medium A? How does the velocity of light vary with change in the optical density of the media?

items.subject: Science
items.text: Which liquid fills the space between eye lens and retina?

items.subject: Science
items.text: Using magnesium ribbon and sulphur powder, describe an activity to show that metal oxides are basic and oxides of non-metals are acidic in nature.

items.subject: Science
items.text:
During the reaction of some metals with dilute hydrochloric acid, following observations were made.
(a) Silver metal does not show any change
(b) The temperature of the reaction mixture rises when aluminium (Al) is added.
(c) The reaction of sodium metal is found to be highly explosive
(d) Some bubbles of a gas are seen when lead (Pb) is reacted with the acid.
Explain these observations giving suitable reasons.

items.subject: Science
items.text: (a) Giving two examples, justify the statement that the sex of the offspring in all animals is not always genetically determined. (b) Differentiate between the sex chromosomes of male and female human beings.

items.subject: Science
items.text: In a bisexual flower inspite of the young stamens being removed artificially, the flower produces fruit. Provide a suitable explanation for the above situation.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Two tangents PQ and PR are drawn from an external point P to a circle with centre O. Prove that QORP is a cyclic quadrilateral.

items.subject: Maths
items.text: Areas of two circles are equal. Is it necessary that their circumferences are equal? Why?
